name: Asthma Basics & Types
cards: Asthma is what kind of obstruction?
Reversible airflow obstruction from chronic airway inflammation.
Which phase of breathing is hardest in asthma?
Excessive bronchoconstriction to a trigger a normal airway ignores.

Negative skin tests, normal immunoglobulin E.

Medication triggers to avoid in asthma?
During or within 3 minutes after exercise.
Peaks at 10 to 15 minutes; resolves by 60 minutes.
Regular inhaled corticosteroid; short-acting beta-2 agonist before exercise.

cards: How often is spirometry repeated to monitor asthma?
Bronchial provocation testing is not recommended when?
Morning before and afternoon after the bronchodilator.
Peak flow change that means poor control?
20% change, morning to afternoon or day to day.
May be absent; only decreased breath sounds.
Night symptoms peak at what time?
2 or fewer days a week; 2 or fewer nights a month.
More than 2 days a week but not daily; 3 to 4 nights a month.
Daily; more than once a week but not nightly.
Throughout the day; often 7 a week.
Which category is assigned when features differ?
The most severe category in which any feature occurs.
